method_limits: a writer is a CALL that puts bytes at a path argument (open in a writing mode, mkdir, to_csv/to_parquet/to_json/to_excel/to_pickle/to_feather, write_text/write_bytes/touch, copy/move destination, replace/rename destination) whose path expression resolves statically; a site that merely NAMES the directory is a reader and is not counted, which is the whole discriminator between this face and E435/E441

resolution is static: literals, module-scope string constants, os.path.join chains, f-string literal heads and constant concatenation. A path built from a loop variable, a function parameter or a json field is unresolved and published as unresolved_write_sites_naming_the_base when its literal head sits under the base -- it is never counted as a writer

the corpus is every .py under the repo root minus ['.codely-cli', '.git', 'Money02', '__pycache__', '_quarantine', '_smoke', 'legacy', 'node_modules'] and this study's own faces; files over 2097152 bytes are skipped and named in corpus.skipped_over_max_bytes

existence of a writer does NOT mean the code still runs: a writer inside a retired script, a test, or a lane guard that no-ops on this machine is still a writer. This face answers 'would anything write there', not 'is anything scheduled to'

the population is E441's published frozen subset, read from its summary; this study never re-grades the base itself, so a base that went live between the two readings is reported through distance_check.agrees instead of being folded in

a base that CONTAINS another published base (this population's `results` contains `results/shortline` and 49 more) is credited with every write anywhere below it. That is what a write into the directory means, but such a row cannot be abandoned by definition, so the population excluding ancestor bases is published next to the full one and both verdicts are printed
member identity in E441 is working-tree mtime, so both faces are readings of the working tree and not of git history

distance_check.reading: the population is read from E441's own summary; a base that changed class between E441 and this reading shows up as agree=false rather than being silently re-graded

title: for each face-home base E441 published as frozen, search the corpus for a write site whose target statically resolves into that base, and publish per base whether a writer exists, where it is, and whether the base is dormant or abandoned
